chapter: Billy Berg's, Granz and Nat Cole
title: Billy Berg's: shared bills and the Blanton, Christian, Hampton jam
summary: He recalls Slim and Slam, Billie Holiday and Spirits of Rhythm on the same bill, and a night when Blanton, Charlie Christian and Hampton jammed.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Billie Holiday as the musicians knew her

blocks.x: We were talking about what happened at Billy Berg's and how Strayhorn brought us "A Train" actually before Duke ever played it. But Billy Berg's was such a fantastic place; I don't know whether we really realized it at the time. But during this period, Slim and Slam worked there, Billie Holiday, Leo Watson, Teddy Bunn and the Spirits of Rhythm, and we were working at the same time.
You mean all on the same bill.

Yeah, on the same bill. Like, Slim and Slam would do a set, then we'd play for Billie Holiday and Prez. And during this time, a lot of jam sessions used to happen. I remember one night Blanton came in, Charlie Christian came in, and Lionel Hampton. So naturally, I got off the stand

and handed my bass to Blanton, and Lionel got up and played the two-finger piano that he does, and Charlie Christian got his guitar... Because this is when both of them were with Benny Goodman, right?

Well, I can remember just sitting there being enthralled with both Charlie Christian and Jimmy Blanton. Because Charlie Christian was about 22 or so, the same age as Blanton -- and I had never heard such wild music.
Yeah. Now, I know there was no wire recording or no aircheck of any of this, but I heard it. It only remains in my memory.
